# Gale

An API-first fan control daemon for Linux.

[![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/Garulf/gale)](https://github.com/Garulf/gale/blob/main/LICENSE) [![version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.1.0-informational)](https://github.com/Garulf/gale)

## Installation

Build and install the daemon and CLI as a systemd service:

```sh
sudo packaging/install.sh
sudo systemctl enable --now galed.service
```

This installs `galed` and `gale` to `/usr/local/bin`, the systemd unit, and the
udev rules that grant hidraw access to supported Corsair devices. Uninstall
with `sudo packaging/install.sh --uninstall`.

### Windows

Download `gale-windows-x86_64.zip` from the
[latest release](https://github.com/Garulf/gale/releases/latest), extract it,
then from an elevated PowerShell in that folder:

```powershell
.\install.ps1
```

This registers `galed` as a Windows service and starts it, and registers a
tray icon that starts with your session and shows the service status.
Uninstall with:

```powershell
.\install.ps1 -Uninstall
```

Windows motherboard (Super I/O) fan control is not yet supported; it lands in
the next release. Corsair and NVIDIA GPU control work today.

## Usage

### Features

- Curve-driven fan control over hwmon (motherboard/CPU headers) and four Corsair
  device families: Commander Core, Commander Pro, Corsair PSU, and Hydro Platinum
- NVIDIA GPU fan control via NVML
- A REST and WebSocket API served alongside an embedded web UI, no separate
  frontend to install
- Curve types: point, trigger, target, flat, mix, and sync
- Journaled claims so a killed daemon restores prior fan state on the next start

### Quick start

`galed` reads its config from the path in `GALE_CONFIG` (default
`/etc/gale/config.toml`). A minimal config assigning a point curve to a
motherboard PWM header:

```toml
tick_interval_ms = 200
active_profile = "default"

[api]
bind = "127.0.0.1:5250"

[profiles.default.curves.cpu]
type = "point"
sensor = "hwmon/nct6798/temp1"
points = [[30.0, 20.0], [70.0, 100.0]]

[profiles.default.assignments]
"hwmon/nct6798/pwm1" = "cpu"
```

Start the daemon (or `systemctl start galed` once installed) and open
`http://127.0.0.1:5250` for the dashboard and curve editor, or drive it with
the `gale` CLI.

### API

The daemon exposes REST and WebSocket endpoints under `/api`, all guarded by
an optional API key set in `[api] api_key`:

| Method | Path                      | Description                          |
| ------ | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| GET    | `/api/status`             | Daemon status                        |
| GET    | `/api/inventory`          | Detected sensors and controls        |
| GET    | `/api/config`             | Current config                       |
| PUT    | `/api/config`             | Replace and reload the config        |
| GET    | `/api/warnings`           | Non-fatal startup and runtime issues |
| POST   | `/api/profiles/:name/activate` | Switch the active profile       |
| PUT    | `/api/controls/*id`       | Set a manual override duty           |
| DELETE | `/api/controls/*id`       | Clear a manual override              |
| GET    | `/api/ws`                 | WebSocket stream of live sensor/control state |

## Hardware support

| Family                | Status                          |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| hwmon (motherboard/CPU) | supported                       |
| Corsair Commander Core  | supported, runtime-unverified against real hardware |
| Corsair Commander Pro   | supported, runtime-unverified against real hardware |
| Corsair PSU             | supported, runtime-unverified against real hardware |
| Corsair Hydro Platinum  | supported, runtime-unverified against real hardware |
| NVIDIA GPU (NVML)       | supported, runtime-unverified against real hardware |
| Nuvoton NCT67xx Super I/O (Windows, PawnIO) | supported, only NCT6798D targeted, runtime-unverified against real hardware |

### Release semantics

Not every backend can return a control to automatic hardware behavior the
same way:

- Commander Core and Corsair PSU restore hardware auto mode when a control is
  released.
- Commander Pro and Hydro Platinum have no unset available upstream, so what
  happens on release there is configurable via `[hardware.corsair]
  on_release` in the config: `"pin_full"` writes 100%, `"keep_last"` leaves
  the last duty in place, and `{ fixed = <percent> }` writes a fixed duty.
  The default is `"keep_last"`.
- On Hydro Platinum, the first `set_duty` call also pins the sibling fans on
  the same device to 100% and the pump to its balanced curve, since the
  protocol addresses the whole device rather than one channel.
- Getting a Commander Pro or Hydro Platinum back onto an iCUE hardware
  profile after Gale has been driving it needs a power cycle or iCUE itself;
  none of the `on_release` modes hand control back to firmware curves.
